items.summary: SimpleOPD: on-policy distillation for long-context reasoning, training-free method for tokenizer-agnostic knowledge transfer. Research on efficient model compression.

items.title: Modular Cognitive Architecture Emerges in Large Language Models
items.snippet: The human brain exhibits a striking degree of functional specialization, with distinct networks supporting language, formal reasoning, reasoning about other minds, and reasoning about the physical world. items.summary: Modular Cognitive Architecture in LLMs: evidence that LLMs develop specialized functional networks. Research on LLM internal organization and interpretability.

items.title: An Empirical Study of Training Pixel-Space Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
items.snippet: This paper investigates an increasingly important topic in generative modeling: pixel-space diffusion models. Although numerous studies have explored this topic, most focus on small-scale or class-conditional settings. Consequently, a practical recipe for training pixel-space models that rival or exceed well-established latent-space counterparts remains elusive. Through a comprehensive empirical s
items.summary: Empirical study of training pixel-space text-to-image diffusion models. Practical training recipe for generative models at scale.

items.title: R^3-Bench: LLMs Struggle with Resource-Rational Reasoning under Shared Budgets
items.snippet: In cognitive science, resource rationality asks how an agent should allocate limited computation to maximize expected value. Most reasoning and agent benchmarks use independent per-task budgets; existing shared-budget studies do not calibrate suite performance against the same model's demonstrated single-problem competence. We introduce R^3-Bench, which evaluates six-problem suites under shared bu
items.summary: R³-Bench: evaluates LLM resource-rational reasoning under shared budgets. Benchmark highlighting reasoning cost allocation challenges.

items.title: Claim-Level Reliability Assessment for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning
items.snippet: We propose claim-level falsification as a principle for test-time scaling and instantiate it through Claim-Level Reliability Assessment (CLR), a training-free framework that reallocates test-time compute from additional solution sampling to targeted verification. Since whole-trace evaluation often obscures decisive errors due to signal dilution from routine tokens, CLR condenses each reasoning tra
items.summary: Claim-Level Reliability Assessment (CLR): training-free test-time scaling via targeted verification instead of sampling. Efficient inference optimization.

items.title: LittleLearner: Language Models Under Pedagogically Controlled Knowledge Exposure
items.snippet: Modern language models are trained on heterogeneous web-scale text corpora. Consequently, studying knowledge and skill acquisition is difficult, as prior exposure to related content is hard to characterize. items.summary: LittleLearner: controlled 88B-token pretraining curriculum to study knowledge acquisition in language models. Research methodology for understanding LLM learning.

items.summary: Method for detecting RAG poisoning attacks via document-level attention collapse. Improves RAG security for production deployments.
